sources.title: Human History Map, historical basemap record for laos-1938
sources.note: Original project record and imported border snapshots checked. The record is circa 1938 to open; geometry appears in 1938, 1960, 1994, 2000 and 2010 snapshots, is absent in 1945, and repeatedly includes the test point Nong Khai in Thailand. These are atlas limitations, not historical boundary claims.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Laos: A Country Study
sources.note: Institutional country study checked for the protectorate, wartime rupture, postwar restoration, 1953 treaty, 1954 Geneva settlement, competing coalitions and the 1975 revolutionary transition. It is a secondary historical synthesis and dated contemporary sections are not used as current conditions.

sources.title: U.S. Office of the Historian, A Guide to the United States History of Recognition and Relations with Laos
sources.note: Official diplomatic chronology checked: French protectorate, independence within the French Union in 1949, United States recognition on 7 February 1950, proclamation of the Lao PDR in December 1975 and later diplomatic changes. Recognition by one country is not presented as the sole act that created Laos.

sources.title: United Nations, List of former Trust and Non-Self-Governing Territories
sources.note: Official UN decolonization table checked. It lists Indochina and independence as Laos, now the Lao People's Democratic Republic, in 1949. The table is used only for that broad decolonization milestone.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Collection, Historical Information: Lao People's Democratic Republic
sources.note: Official historical-name note checked: Lao People's Democratic Republic was formerly Laos until 22 December 1975. This treaty-depository note supports name continuity, not a complete political history.

sources.title: World Bank, Lao PDR Economic Monitor, November 2004
sources.note: Original report checked for the 1975 socialization programme and the 1986 New Economic Mechanism: price liberalization, exchange-rate unification, removal of the trade monopoly, entry of private firms, encouragement of family farms and reduction of state enterprises. World Bank evaluation is attributed and not treated as neutral proof of every outcome.

sources.title: World Bank, Lao Economic Monitor, June 2026: Consolidating Reform Momentum Amid Volatility
sources.note: Current institutional assessment checked: 4.8 percent growth in 2025, tourism, transport and electricity-related exports, renewed fuel-price pressure, debt vulnerability, household welfare and constraints on public health financing. Recommendations and projections are identified as such.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Megalithic Jar Sites in Xiengkhuang, Plain of Jars
sources.note: Official World Heritage entry checked: more than 2,100 megalithic jars; 15 property components; jars, discs, burials, quarries and grave goods; funerary use and dates about 500 BCE to 500 CE. This ancient evidence is not attributed to the modern state.

sources.title: UNDP Lao PDR, International Mine Awareness Day, 4 April 2025
sources.note: Original UNDP release checked: Second Indochina War legacy, more than two million items destroyed including 1.2 million submunitions, 949 square kilometres cleared, 49 casualties in 2024 and more than 60 percent of casualties children. Numbers are dated and clearance progress is not equated with removing all danger.

sources.title: FAO, Lao PDR Census of Agriculture 2019/2020, Rice Production
sources.note: Official agriculture-census report checked: sticky rice was 84 percent of rainy-season rice production and 96 percent of dry-season production in 2019/20; much rice was retained for consumption. These are production statistics, not a claim that every person eats the same food.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Khaen music of the Lao people
sources.note: Official 2017 inscription checked: bamboo mouth organ with metal reeds; village festivals; listeners joining songs and dances; family and association transmission; family and social cohesion. UNESCO inscription describes a living practice, not every household.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Traditional craft of Naga motif weaving in Lao communities
sources.note: Official 2023 inscription checked: mythical river Naga, hand weaving on wooden looms, motif formed during weaving rather than printed or embroidered, family transmission, and use on infant cloths, wedding clothing, daily dress and funerary textiles. Beliefs are reported as community traditions, not scientific claims.

sources.title: UNICEF Lao PDR, Education
sources.note: Official programme page checked for barriers faced by children in remote and non-Lao-speaking communities, the Lao language of instruction, community-based school readiness, parent education, teacher support and the need for safe school WASH facilities. Older percentages are not repeated as current figures.

sources.title: UNICEF Lao PDR, In Lao PDR, a digital transformation of education has begun
sources.note: Original 2022 field report checked: digital-literacy camp, tablets and online safety; Khang Panya Lao national platform and Lao-language curriculum resources; low access to devices, electricity and affordable stable internet. Participant experience is not generalized to all schools.

sources.title: WHO Lao PDR, Safeguarding maternal, newborn and child health
sources.note: Official WHO programme account checked: Early Essential Newborn Care, Kangaroo Mother Care, skin-to-skin contact, breastfeeding, medical-school assessment, integrated child services and community CONNECT work. It also says preventable deaths and quality gaps remain.

sources.title: WHO Lao PDR, Lao PDR makes significant strides in measles prevention
sources.note: Official 1 November 2024 account checked: May campaign target 633,849 children in 148 districts; more than 603,000 vaccinated, or 95.2 percent of the target; vitamin A also administered. WHO cautions that campaign numbers cannot simply be added to routine national coverage.

sources.title: UNICEF Lao PDR, Good Hygiene Practices begin at school
sources.note: Original 5 August 2019 field story checked at Doub Primary in Saravane: pupil-led group handwashing, toilet use and cleaning, filtered water, peer demonstrations, parent involvement and the teacher's observation that pupils chatted while scrubbing. One school is an example, not a national average.

sources.title: UNICEF Lao PDR, Clean water reaches Phangsane village in Phongsaly
sources.note: Original 26 January 2023 field report checked: 52-household Yao community, household taps from a gravity-fed system, local labour and fees, WASH committee, toilets in every household, time saved from fetching water and new gardening opportunities. This is one documented village.

sources.title: U.S. Foreign Service Institute, Everyday Lao, Lesson 1
sources.note: Public-domain Foreign Service Institute instructional book checked in the preserved PDF. Lesson 1 prints ສະບາຍດີ and translates it as Hello. The phrase is a modern instructional sample, not an ancient inscription or proof that all residents use Lao in every setting.

proposedOverrides.summary: Modern Laos from protectorate and staged independence to the continuing Lao PDR, with ancient jars, sticky rice, living arts, schools, medicine, sanitation and UXO recovery.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Treat as the modern-territory Laos record only. The index is circa 1938 to open, but politics change from French protectorate to independent Kingdom of Laos and then the Lao People's Democratic Republic in December 1975. Geometry is present in world-1938, absent in world-1945, and next present in world-1960, creating an actual 1945 to 1960 atlas-coverage gap even though the chronology is open. Later stored outlines begin in 1994, 2000 and 2010. All decoded outlines include Vientiane, Luang Prabang, Pakse, Savannakhet, Phonsavan, Attapeu and Luang Namtha, but also include the Nong Khai test point across the Mekong in Thailand, so the border is disclosed as approximate. Do not alias to the separate laos or laos-1800 records, Lan Xang, Luang Prabang, Vientiane or other earlier Lao polities. Independence is described in stages: 1949 status within the French Union, final treaty restrictions removed in 1953, sovereign participation at Geneva in 1954, and republican transformation in 1975. No invented fall or successor.
